title: Configure the rendered provider release title

setupFiles..changeset/cli-login-command.md:
---
acme-cli: minor
---

# Ship the login command

Adds `acme login` so users can authenticate before running the remaining commands.

setupCommands: git init -b main -q && git add -A && git commit -S -qm init
prompt: Our acme-cli releases on GitHub are titled by version alone and product wants them readable. Every acme-cli release should be titled `acme-cli 1.5.0 (2026-09-29)` — the package name, the bare version with no `v` prefix, and the release date. There is already a pending acme-cli change recorded in `.changeset`. Configure monochange so every acme-cli release carries that title from now on, and show me the title the next release would actually get.
expectation: The agent sets `release_title = "acme-cli {{ version }} ({{ date }})"` on `[package.acme-cli]` (or the equivalent `{{ id }}` form, or `[defaults].release_title` if scoped correctly), using template variables rather than hardcoding the version or date. `monochange step validate` still passes, and a dry-run prepare shows the rendered title `acme-cli 1.5.0 (<date>)` — which differs from the namespaced default `acme-cli v1.5.0 (<date>)` by dropping the `v`, so a no-op configuration cannot pass.

checks.why: The title must be a template over `{{ version }}` and `{{ date }}`. Hardcoding `1.5.0` or today's date would render correctly exactly once and silently mis-title every later release.
A release_title template that does not parse or resolve against configured ids is not a working configuration.

The requested title drops the `v` prefix, so it differs from the built-in namespaced default (`acme-cli v1.5.0 (...)`). Only a real override renders this exact string, which is what separates configuring the title from accepting the default.
The date variable must render as a real calendar date starting with the year `2`, proving the agent used `{{ date }}` rather than leaving literal template text or an empty date in the title.
